claims.text: Conventional thermomechanical processing can improve metal strength at the cost of reduced ductility.
Traditional treatments yield comparatively homogeneous microstructures through conventional grain refinement or precipitation hardening.
A machine-learning framework using high-throughput experimental data can predict optimal temperature profiles, deformation parameters, reduction ratios, and aging times.
ML-optimized thermomechanical processing will produce tailored dual-phase microstructures.
The tailored microstructures will contain multiple coherent precipitation interfaces.
Selected processing-parameter combinations will foster nanoscale precipitates with coherent boundaries and fine grains.
Nanoscale coherent precipitates and fine grains will impede dislocation motion.
The optimized microstructural features will promote uniform plastic deformation.
The combined effects of impeded dislocation motion and uniform plastic deformation will synergistically enhance strength and ductility.
ML-guided processing will improve yield strength relative to conventional processing.
ML-guided processing will improve ductility relative to conventional processing.
The proposed approach is applicable to metallic systems under ambient and standard thermomechanical conditions.
